assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.

The analysis period is 17 Sep 2026, compared with the immediately preceding period of equal length (16 Sep 2026); the anomaly detection and segment analysis widened the window to 17-18 Sep versus 10-16 Sep.
caveats: The comparison window runs 17-18 Sep versus 10-16 Sep, so the figures cover two days of impact, not 17 Sep alone.
The hourly timeline for Kestrel Bank cards is only partly shown in the evidence (16 Sep), so the exact start and end of the incident cannot be confirmed from what was provided.
The hour-of-day view shows the overall rate across both days combined, so it does not by itself pin down when on 17 Sep the problem began.

facts.text: Attempt success rate fell 3.10pp, from 90.1% (10-16 Sep, 83,268 attempts) to 87.0% (17-18 Sep, 22,790 attempts). The change is statistically and practically significant.

The segment scan ranks acquirer as the dimension that most concentrates the drop. Kestrel Bank's success rate fell 11.54pp, from 90.0% to 78.5%. Northstar Bank (-0.44pp), Meridian Bank (+0.27pp) and Saffron Bank (+0.24pp) showed no significant change.

Within Kestrel Bank, three card methods fell sharply and significantly: debit card fell 30.11pp (86.4% to 56.3%), credit card fell 28.71pp (88.6% to 59.9%) and card EMI fell 23.87pp (80.7% to 56.8%). UPI, wallet and netbanking were not significantly changed.

For Kestrel Bank card payments, ACQ_TIMEOUT failures rose from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts (803 failures in the current window versus 22 in the baseline). Issuer declines, risk declines and customer drop-off codes all moved by less than 1 per 100 attempts.

Across all payments, ACQ_TIMEOUT rose from 0.08 to 3.58 per 100 attempts (815 failures in the current window versus 69 in the baseline). No other failure code moved by more than 0.16 per 100 attempts.
The hourly view of overall success rate shows significant drops versus baseline in hours 11-15 and 17-23. Hours 0-10 were not significantly different.
The data-quality scan found no issues (0 findings).

response.headline: Yes. Success rate fell 3.10pp from 90.1% to 87.0% over 17-18 Sep versus the prior week, and the drop is concentrated in card payments routed through Kestrel Bank, where acquirer timeouts spiked.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check Kestrel Bank's incident or status notices for 17-18 Sep, and review the hourly start and end times of the timeout spike against their change or maintenance log.
hypotheses.rationale: The drop is isolated to one acquirer and to its card methods only, while UPI, wallet and netbanking at the same acquirer were unaffected. The failure-code shift is almost entirely ACQ_TIMEOUT, a technical acquirer code, and other acquirers were flat.
hypotheses.text: An acquirer-side technical incident at Kestrel Bank (for example connectivity or processing degradation on its card rails) caused card authorisations to time out.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Hypothesis: acquirer-side technical incident at Kestrel Bank
recommendations.rationale: The evidence points to an acquirer-side technical failure limited to one acquirer's card traffic.
recommendations.text: Raise the incident with Kestrel Bank, citing the card-method timeouts, and ask for a root-cause analysis and the exact start and end times.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Facts on Kestrel Bank card-method declines and ACQ_TIMEOUT spike
recommendations.rationale: Other acquirers showed no significant change, and Kestrel's card success rate fell to roughly 56-60%.
recommendations.text: Consider routing card traffic away from Kestrel Bank to healthy acquirers, or enabling fallback or retry to another acquirer, if the timeouts are still ongoing.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Fact: ACQ_TIMEOUT spike for Kestrel Bank card payments
recommendations.rationale: The spike went from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts for Kestrel cards, which an alert would catch early.
recommendations.text: Set an alert on ACQ_TIMEOUT per 100 attempts by acquirer and payment method.
